content.content:
## Cyrus studios UI (R1b)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r5` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). The studio shell, the mod **Assets** tab, the locked states, the shared **Library browser** and the full **Texture Studio**, built from the approved mockups (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/`: texture-studio, mod-assets, locked-states; implementation shots in `impl-shots/`). **Nothing is deployed. The new setting `cyrus_studios_enabled` is OFF**: until the owner turns it on only preview accounts see any of it, so nothing changes for customers.

### Gates (all server side; the UI only shows the result)
- **Visibility** (`lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts studiosOpen`, `deps.ts studioViewer`): a Cyrus user (`modBuilderUser`: preview, or the public launch) AND (a preview account OR `cyrus_studios_enabled`). Anyone else gets the normal 404 page / API 404. Setting registered in `lib/settings.ts` and the admin settings catalog (default `false`).
- **Plan** (`studioPlanView` = engine-core `canAsset`): Texture Studio + Texture Library = the top plan `all` ("All models", it includes Yakko); Sound Studio + Sound Library = Saka and up; Free / Katara none. Only create/edit is gated: a mod's assets are always listed and viewable (locked pages show them read only). An unknown plan (lookup error) fails closed for editing, never for viewing. Every write handler re-runs the gate.

### Owner defaults for the open design questions (`STUDIO_DEFAULTS` in `lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts`)
| Question | Default now |
|---|---|
| Plan names | exactly the code's: Free, Katara, Saka, All models (Yakko is the top model) |
| Token cost on asset edits | shown in the prompt dock (`CyrusTokenEstimate`, change build on Yakko) |
| Packs on join | optional (`required: false`); the per-mod "required" flag is the Pack Loader entry's |
| Mob skin | shown as "Mob skin · coming soon", not hidden |
| Mobile | read-only preview + approve / reject (approving saves a revision) |
| Editor placement | full page (`/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/texture`), quick entry from the inspector's Assets tab |

### Routes and files
- Pages: `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/texture` (editor; plans that may not edit get the locked state in place), `.../studio/sound` (locked / included states only: the Sound Studio editor is the next slice), `.../studio/plans?studio=texture|sound` (locked / included / plan-unknown + plan matrix). `app/dashboard/cyrus/studio-shared.tsx` = gates + crumb data. `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>?tab=assets` opens the inspector on Assets.
- API (versioned, all `/api/cyrus/assets/v1`, thin wrappers over `lib/cyrus/studios/http.ts`): `GET projects?root=` (assets, access, pack, revision seqs, candidate summaries), `GET|POST projects/:p/textures/:key/revisions` (history / save as a NEW revision), `POST quality`, `POST projects/:p/textures/:key/candidates`, `GET .../candidates/:id` (poll), `POST .../candidates/:id/reject`, `GET library` (browse), `POST library/use`, `POST library/upload` (multipart), `GET library/asset/:id/png`, `GET projects/:p/pack`. Every handler: viewer -> per-user rate limit -> input validation -> plan gate (writes) -> service. Errors are JSON `{ error, code }`.
- Libraries: `lib/cyrus/studios/{paint,editor,access,held,marker}.ts` (pure, client-safe), `service.ts` (logic over injected deps), `http.ts` (handlers), `deps.ts` (the ONLY file reaching Nxeon seams: modBuilderUser + preview list, settings, tokens `tierOf`, rate limiter), `store-prisma.ts` (Cyrus tables via engine-core store + the ModBuild chain, read only), `candidates.ts` (real change-build backend), `uploads.ts`. `lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts` (item display transforms).
- UI: `components/cyrus/studios/` (`StudioShell`, `TextureStudio`, `LibraryBrowser`, `StudioLock` + `PlanMatrix`, `AssetsTab`, `studios.css`, `icons.tsx` = the mockup's icon set). Hooked in: `PreviewPanel` (Assets tab only when the server opened the studios, real mods only), `CyrusApp`/`shared.tsx` (`studios` prop, `?tab=assets`), `lib/cyrus/store.ts` (`studios`, PanelTab `assets`). Also fixed: `CyrusApp` read `realBuilds` from the store snapshot taken before `setReal`, so `/dashboard/cyrus/<id>` deep links never selected the mod.
- No new tables, no migration.

### Paint-layer persistence (decision)
A studio texture is a **TextureDoc** (`lib/cyrus/studios/paint.ts`): the locked generated base (an ordinary DSL `TextureSpec`, still bounded by `MAX_OPS` 400) + an optional **sparse paint layer** `{ size, colors[<=256 "#rrggbb"], set: [pixel, colourIndex, ...] sorted, clear: [pixel, ...] }` (+ `tile` profile, `supersedes`, `decision`). Painting never becomes DSL ops, so the 400-op limit does not apply to strokes (a full 64x64 paint is valid; tested). The doc is stored with the asset (`CyrusProjectAsset`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.texture-doc+json`, provenance `{ doc, quality, pngSha256, basedOn, packSha1 }`, sha256 = canonical JSON) and **composited everywhere pixels matter**: canvas, quality checks (`docQuality` = `tq-1` on the composite), PNG, and the pack (`buildPack` accepts docs as well as specs). Paint is opaque only; erase = clear to alpha 0. An uploaded PNG used in a project becomes an all-paint doc (`spec: null`).
- **Saving** = a new `CyrusRevision` (kind `asset`, status `passed`, `expectedHeadId` optimistic lock -> 409 `stale_head`) whose manifest is the head's with `assets/textures/<key>.json` replaced, plus a new asset row (content-addressed). Revisions and rows are never edited. A failing composite (quality `fail`) is refused (422). If the mod's pack carries no sounds, the pack is rebuilt from every current doc and published through the existing pack store (`selectPackStore`; off = "built, not hosted"); packs with sounds are rebuilt by the next build (said in the toast). **Not wired:** pushing a studio-saved pack to servers (delivery reads `ModBuild.result.assets`); the next build ships it.
- **Builds keep studio edits** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` optional `studioDocFor`, wired in `sync-deps.ts`): when a build returns a texture spec that the current studio doc *supersedes* (the generated spec it was edited from, or a candidate the customer rejected / accepted), the doc (spec + paint) goes into the pack and the asset row (origin `edited`, `keptStudioEdit`). If the build changed that texture, the build's spec wins and the studio edit stays in history. Without the dep, sync is byte-identical to before (tested).

### Candidates (the AI edit interface)
`CandidateBackend { request({ user, project, chain, key, prompt, current }) -> requestId; poll(...) -> pending | ready { doc, specSha256, summary } | failed }` (`lib/cyrus/studios/service.ts`). Real: `changeBuildCandidates` (`candidates.ts`) = `createModBuild(user, { baseBuildId: newest succeeded build, changeRequest: 'Texture Studio edit of "<key>": <prompt> ...', assets: ["texture"], model: "yakko" })` (plan + token gates of the normal flow); its texture row, recorded by the normal asset sync, is the candidate. Candidate builds are recognised by that change-request marker (`marker.ts`), are never "current", and are listed until a studio revision records a decision (`doc.decision`). Accept = save with `acceptCandidate` (server re-reads the candidate's spec sha; never trusts the client); partial = chosen changed-pixel regions (8-connected, `changeRegions`) or the selection are written into the paint layer; reject = a revision that keeps the current doc and records the decision (and supersedes the candidate spec, so a later build that still carries it keeps the customer's texture). **Fake**: `fakeCandidates` (deterministic Style-DNA edit; `CYRUS_STUDIO_CANDIDATES=fake`, non-production only). The real backend was NOT run (no paid model calls). Note for the owner: a real candidate is a new mod version in Versions (the change-build flow); rejecting it does not delete that build.

### In-hand preview and the pack's display block
The pack now writes an explicit `display` block into every item model (`lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts displayFor`): tools/weapons get the game's own `item/handheld` values (first-person right hand rotation [0,-90,25] translation [1.13,3.2,1.13] scale 0.68; third-person [0,-90,55] / [0,4,0.5] / 0.85; left hands mirrored), verified 2026-10-10 against the Minecraft 1.21.4 asset mirror (github.com/InventivetalentDev/minecraft-assets, models/item/handheld.json and generated.json; numbers only, no Mojang asset committed). Handguns (name match: glock, pistol, gun, revolver, ...) are drawn side-on, so they get Cyrus rotations (`GUN_ROTATION`: first person [-10,150,30], third person [0,90,10]) and a translation re-gripped so their grip (documented default: centre of the opaque pixels in the lowest 40 % within the left 60 %) sits where vanilla holds a tool's handle (texel 2,14). No texture marks a grip anchor yet; the defaults are per category. The studio's "In hand" view (first / third person, right hand) applies the SAME transforms (`lib/cyrus/studios/held.ts`) to the extruded item and draws a brand-violet glove + sleeve whose fist closes over the grip. The hand position, camera and arm are Cyrus's approximation of the game renderer, so the panel says **approximate**; the handgun rotations are UNVERIFIED in a real client (check on the client test day). Hotbar and Tile previews are unchanged from the mockup.

### Sound Studio plug-in points (next slice)
- Page: render the editor in `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/sound/page.tsx` when `plan.edit.sound.ok` (today it renders `StudioLock studio="sound"`), inside `StudioShell studio="sound"` (crumbs, Texture/Sound switch, toast via `useToast`).
- Library: `<LibraryBrowser kind="sound" projectId onUse renderLead />` (`renderLead` = the audition button; `onUse` posts to `library/use`). `handleUse` currently answers 400 "Sound library picks arrive with the Sound Studio" for `sound/*` refs: add the `useSoundFromLibrary` branch there (and the `libraryCleared` flag).
- Locked states, plan matrix and build notices for sound already work (`StudioLock`, `buildNotices`). Data: `GET projects?root=` already returns `sounds` (the build's `MbAssets.sounds`) and `soundRender`.

### Tests (RAN on node-2 via devhost)
- `test/cyrus-studios.test.ts` (35: paint layer round trip / composite / validation / 64x64 beyond 400 ops; pack ships the composite + display blocks; quality on the composite; held transforms incl. re-grip invariants and gun direction; editor history / tools / regions / ramps; gates per plan; service on an in-memory store: new revision, stale head, quality refusal, plan gate per plan, candidates + reject; sync merge (kept / replaced / no dep); API handlers with fakes: 404 / 429 / 400, save + history, candidate request -> poll -> accept, browse (gated for Saka) + use-in-project, uploads 503 off / 201 on + use, quality endpoint). With the other Cyrus suites: 261/261. `test/cyrus.test.ts` 45/45. `devhost tsc` clean.
- Full suite: 53 failures, all in areas this branch does not touch (pricing/proration, admin guards, billing scanners, registrar guard, ...) except the Cyrus page-gate scanner, which this branch fixed (studio pages call `requireModBuilderUser()` first).
- Playwright interaction tests `test/e2e/cyrus-studios.e2e.mjs` (24/24 passed: pencil stroke = one step, paint count, undo / redo shortcuts, tool keys, fake candidate as a split compare layer, accept, save, history after reload, library "use in project", narrow review + approve, Katara narrow lock, Saka locked + API 403, Saka sound included, Free sound locked, plan-unknown fails closed with assets visible, non-preview account not-found + API 404). Screenshots `test/e2e/cyrus-studios.shots.mjs` -> `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/` (24). How to run: the header of both scripts (fixtures `scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts`, devhost throwaway DB only; env `CYRUS_STUDIO_CANDIDATES=fake CYRUS_UPLOAD_STORE=local CYRUS_STUDIO_TEST_PLAN_UNKNOWN=usr_studio_unknown CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` for the "hosted" pack state).
- NOT RUN: the real change-build candidate backend (paid model), real pack hosting / delivery, a real Minecraft client (display transforms in game), production upload storage (none exists; uploads are 503 there).

### Remaining gaps vs the mockups (honest)
- The real portal frame (248 px sidebar + portal top bar) leaves less width than the mockup's 60 px rail; the 1180 px container rule tightens the columns. The portal's floating help bubble overlaps the bottom-right of the right column (the pane has bottom padding so content can scroll above it).

- `search.ts searchAssets / similarAssets`: one query over both kinds with BOTH synonym tables; ranking exact tag 5 (4 via synonym) > use case/category/subcategory/kind 3 > tag prefix 2 > name 1, every word must match, +0.5 each when the word is the subcategory / primary material; filters (kinds, sources, category, subcategory, useCase, tags, descriptors), facets (kind, source, category, subcategory, useCase, size/transparency/tileable/material/durationClass/intensity/pitchBand/quality/moderation), pagination (max 200), "similar" prefers other shapes over recolours.
- `catalog.ts browseLibrary(deps, {userId, projectId, query})` / `similarInLibrary`: `deps = {providers, planOf}`; `planOf` is the host seam (wire it to `lib/cyrus/tokens/access tierOf`, as the DB test does); a throwing lookup = unknown plan. Gated sources are omitted and returned in `denied` (for the upgrade hint).
- `use-in-project.ts`: `useTextureFromLibrary({itemId|templateId, ramps, dna (preset id or the mod's own DnaPreset), key, namespace}, reserve)` -> TextureSpec named `key`, quality report (refuses a failing combination), identifier `<ns>:item/<key>` (`block/<key>` for blocks) reserved through the injected `reserve` (portal: `reserveIdentifier(projectId, "model", path)`), an asset slot (`source: library`) and provenance. `useSoundFromLibrary({id, set, event, role, subtitle, namespace, libraryCleared}, reserve)` -> a valid SoundSpec (layer `lib:<id>`, default pitch -1 so the file never ships unchanged, the licence rule) and `<ns>:<set>.<event>`; refuses unless `libraryCleared` (fail closed, same flag as builds). `soundLayerFrom(id)` for adding a layer to an existing variant.

### 3. Uploads (backend only: `png-decode.ts`, `upload.ts`)
- `validateTextureUpload(bytes, {profile, allowTranslucent})`: 256 KiB cap before parsing; CRC on every chunk; IHDR first; square 16/32/64 only, checked BEFORE inflating; 8-bit grey/RGB/RGBA/grey-alpha and 1-8-bit palette (+tRNS); 16-bit and interlaced refused; inflate capped at the exact size the header implies (decompression bomb -> `decompression_bomb`); unknown critical chunks refused; ancillary chunks reported in `stripped` and dropped because the PNG is RE-ENCODED from pixels (RGB under alpha 0 zeroed); semi-transparent pixels refused by default; > 256 colours refused (photo); quality bar must not fail.
- `uploadTexture(input, deps)`: plan gate (upload = create; texture = top plan), project ownership, head revision required, moderation hook (`moderationStub` = documented stub: everything `unreviewed`, nothing approved; `rejected` stores nothing), content-addressed storage key `cyrus/uploads/<project>/<sha256>.png` via the injected `UploadStorage`, then `recordAsset` (kind texture, origin upload, provenance = name, size, alpha mode, palette, quality report, moderation, stripped chunks, original sha/bytes, customer ledger). **No new table**: the row is recorded against the current head revision (an upload adds to the project's library; it does not change the mod's files). No production storage adapter exists yet.

### 4. Tests (RAN on node-2 via devhost)
`test/cyrus-texture-library.test.ts` + `test/cyrus-library.test.ts` (53 tests; with cyrus-textures/assets/sounds/engine-core 233 pass), `test/cyrus-library-db.test.ts` (opt-in, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_DB_TEST=1` on the throwaway DB: upload -> CyrusProjectAsset idempotent, Prisma store + real `tierOf` gate, other users invisible, real identifier registry). `tsc --noEmit` clean.

- Look at the contact sheets; mark anything to cut. Weakest by the author's own judgement: rubble-stone cracks, log bark (regular), rune tile glyph, scythe/sickle silhouettes, fur swatch, bubble.
- Vanilla near-copy reference set (build-host fingerprints from the server jar) is not built.

The build service pulls its base from the latest build's generated source, not the studio edit, so without pushing the studio spec into the sync path, the next build would just regenerate the old spec. I'll mirror the texture approach with a `studioSoundFor(set)` function returning the spec, hash, and supersedes list, substituting the studio spec when a build's returned spec hash matches something in supersedes—implemented as an optional dependency in sync.ts so it's byte-identical without it, modeled on how studioDocFor is wired into sync.ts and sync-deps.ts.

I'm also sketching out the pure model editing functions—adding/removing/setting layers with range clamps, processing settings, variant management, weights, subtitles, categories, event slots and odds—plus drag operations for manipulating layers directly.

I need a layer extent calculator, subtitle validation matching the spec's rules (length and character restrictions), and a function collecting save blockers across events. For audio, I'm defining peak extraction and diffing functions for waveform display, and a preview cache key based on hashing canonical layer-spec JSON—since hashing needs to happen server-side, I'll keep that in a server-only module rather than the client-safe pure logic.

I'm also working out gating logic: a sound studio gate derived from the plan, and an audition gate that only allows library auditions when cleared and the plan permits sound creation or editing, each needing per-plan unit tests. Finally I'm starting to think through the client-side variant preview renderer.

For library layers, since the raw library audio isn't available client-side, the gated preview route should return a short, cached, processed rendering of just that layer (trimmed, pitched, faded, gain-applied) as compressed audio; the browser decodes it into PCM via WebAudio and mixes it alongside synth layers using the same rest-of-chain processing, effectively treating the server-rendered preview as the layer's "source" in the client pipeline.

Capped to roughly six seconds, this trimmed mono downmix isn't technically the raw file but is close to the raw segment, so to be safer I should also apply the layer's mandatory pitch transform to the preview.

I'd avoid double-applying pitch client-side by baking it into the transformed variant and setting pitch to zero there, letting the client handle fades and gain separately. The cleanest approach is having the host render just the layer alone with its trim, length, pitch, and fades applied, but gain at zero and offset at zero — essentially the layer's full processing chain minus the parts the client controls.

For the preview cache key, I'd hash together the version, library ID, library checksum, trim parameters, length, pitch, fade values, and render version, then cap preview duration at around 8 seconds to keep buffer sizes manageable at 44.1kHz mono.

I'm weighing format options for the audio response: Ogg Vorbis is smaller but has inconsistent decodeAudioData support in Safari, so returning a 16-bit WAV might be the safer, simpler choice despite the larger file size (~705KB for 8 seconds).

I'll cap preview length at 6 seconds, since full layer renders can go up to 8s but a preview role should stay shorter. I'm also thinking about how the existing render host would generate this — reusing the normal RenderJob pipeline would apply loudness normalization and silence trimming that could distort the preview's relative level, so it might be better to introduce a new preview-specific job kind in the runner rather than hijacking the existing variant-rendering path.

Since the audio library only lives on node-2 and access must stay gated, I'm realizing I can't just test this through a browser-facing path — I'd need to either inject a fake render host for dev/tests, or run one real CLI invocation directly on node-2 to validate the actual render without exposing it through any served endpoint.

I'm also now considering how the library audition for a raw item differs from previewing a layer — it seems to play the item as-is with some default trim and pitch settings, which I need to confirm against the devhost setup on node-2.

Settling on audition as a short, trimmed, faded preview job clearly marked as "preview" in the UI.

Now I'm thinking through library peaks: whether to derive coarse amplitude envelopes into committed manifest metadata or fetch them via the gated route. A quantized envelope of ~48 values per file is tiny, non-reconstructable audio, and useful for showing waveform shape in trim UI even when the source is cleared.

For the editor view, when a library layer has no client-side PCM, I'd show its outline from the stored envelope with a note explaining it's an approximation since the real audio is gated off. Generating peaks for all 514 files via ffmpeg on node-2 is a moderate decode job, so I need to check whether devhost can access the library directory, and I'd keep this separate by writing a dedicated `library.peaks.json` file rather than touching the main manifest generation script.

I'm thinking of encoding each peak file as 64 buckets per item, using a single base-36 character per bucket to represent dB level, which keeps the total size around 41KB for all 514 items — small enough to load server-side and attach to each item in browse results. Since this is just metadata like the existing LUFS/duration fields, it's fine to always include it for users who pass the plan gate, since browse access is already gated.

For client-side rendering when there's no actual audio available, substituting silence would throw off the LUFS meters since they'd only measure the synth layers. I'm leaning toward being upfront about this limitation — either labeling the meters as a synth-only estimate, or routing through a "Render and preview" button that calls out to the render host for authoritative measurements, though that raises questions about whether rendering library layers should be gated by the same clearance flag, and whether the studio should even allow saving a spec with uncleared library layers in the first place.

Now I'm tackling SoundStudio.tsx, the most layout-sensitive piece, structuring it as StudioShell wrapping a Body component that handles the empty state—showing the Library with an "Ask Cyrus" hint when there's no project or sound sets yet.

For the Editor, I'm reusing the undo/redo history helpers from editor.ts and designing commit semantics: new edits either coalesce into the current history step (for things like repeated slider drags on the same field) or push a fresh step, dropping any redo tail. Slider inputs coalesce by key/field, while waveform drag operations like trim, move, and fade commit through a similar coalescing scheme keyed to the drag session.

I'm figuring out drag gesture tracking for the waveform editor — using a gesture ref that assigns a coalesce key on the first move event and resets to null when the drag finishes, so subsequent drags start fresh history steps, with labels derived by diffing the layer's properties (start, trim, fade, gain) to describe what changed. I'm also planning keyboard shortcuts (space, L, ctrl+Z/Y), wiring the playhead to the audio position, and letting clicks on the waveform seek playback before moving on to meter computations.

I'm computing measurements and sound quality from the rendered PCM, falling back to "Nothing to measure yet" when empty, and designing a host render state that caches a key (derived from the event spec) alongside the decoded view and PCM so meters and checks reflect host numbers when the spec matches — with play defaulting to the browser mix unless a matching host render exists, in which case a small button lets you play that render instead. For the library tab, I'm wiring an audition button that fetches a preview, decodes it, and plays it.

If the sound isn't licence-cleared, the audition button stays disabled with a truthful explanatory title and toast instead of faking playback — and the "Add" action similarly lets the server reject the request honestly rather than pretending it worked, merging in library metadata only on success. For the history tab, I'm laying out each revision as a row with a mini waveform of that revision's rendering, a diff against the current draft, a label and timestamp, and a Restore button that commits the reverted spec.

For the checks tab, I'm showing a verdict block alongside individual checks, a subtitle check, and a note clarifying whether the estimate came from the browser or the render host.

For candidate flows, asking for a candidate requires the current event to already have variants — I poll the server until a candidate spec is ready, then show it as a selectable "Candidate" chip that swaps the waveform and layers panel into a read-only preview of that candidate's layers (sliders disabled, with a note to accept before editing). I'm also sketching the candidate bar label itself.

Now I'm working out the action buttons on that candidate bar — A/B against V1, Replace V1, Add as V3, Accept all, Reject — and mapping these to the underlying operations (replace_event for "accept all" since the fake data gives one variant, otherwise partial replace/add). I need to trim this button set since the candbar is narrow, maybe only keeping "Replace all" when there's more than one variant.

For the reject flow, I'm distinguishing persisted candidates (where rejection goes through the server to record the decision) from fake/in-memory ones that just get discarded locally, since the fake backend keeps its own request state in memory rather than persisting it.

For the A/B comparison, I'm having it play the original variant then switch to the candidate after a brief 250ms gap. The narrow view lists sets/events alongside the candidate approve/reject controls, and saving runs through blockers first, surfacing a toast for the first one found before calling the save API.

On save, I call studioApi.saveSound with the project, set, spec, baseAssetId, expectedHeadId, and optionally acceptCandidate/mode if accepted, then show a toast confirming the revision number and noting players only hear it after the next build, followed by a reload.

Each set saves independently as its own revision -- the save footer tracks which sets are dirty, and "Save revision" only commits the currently selected one, leaving others listed if still dirty. I also need expectedHeadId to refresh correctly after a save so reload() picks up the new head, and I'm thinking through how an empty "spawn" event selection should behave.

When a slot like spawn is unused, selecting it shows an empty subtitle and waveform with a CTA prompting the user to add a synth preset, library sound, or ask Cyrus -- clicking it alone doesn't create an event, but adding a layer or typing a subtitle does, so I'm building an `ensureEvent()` helper that returns the spec and index. Now I'm sketching the layout structure: CSS classes prefixed `sd-`, header icons distinguishing creature vs item sets, and the event row markup showing the event name with a dimmed role tag and small text.

I'm also planning a save footer for the left panel showing unsaved edit count or last saved revision, undo/redo buttons, a save revision button, and any blocking errors with an explanation that saving creates a new revision for servers to pick up. Now I need to actually write the full TSX carefully, making sure hooks aren't called conditionally.

37/39 tests pass, but one failure is in the peaks roundtrip test — the quantization rounding to 3 decimals introduces disproportionately large dB errors for small amplitude values near the threshold, since the relative error from rounding grows as the value shrinks.

I want to confirm the exact failing assertion line before committing to a fix.

## Cyrus sound studio UI (R1b)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r9` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10), on top of "Cyrus studios UI (R1b)" and "Cyrus sound slice (R1)". The full-page **Sound Studio**, the Sound Library browser with gated audition, sound sets in the mod's Assets tab and in the locked view, all from the approved mockup (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/sound-studio.html`, shots `shots/sound-*`). **Nothing is deployed; `cyrus_studios_enabled` stays OFF** (only preview accounts see it), the library stays OFF (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED` unset) and the render host stays OFF (`CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER` unset): customers see no change.

### Gates (server side; the UI only shows them)
Same as the studios: visibility (`studioViewer`), then the plan (`canAsset(plan, "sound", ...)`): **Sound Studio + Sound Library = Saka and the top plan**; Free / Katara get the locked state in place at `/studio/sound` (the mod's sound events stay listed and playable, read only); an unknown plan fails closed for editing (never for viewing). Every write handler re-runs the gate. Library audition and "Use in project" need BOTH the licence flag and the plan (`auditionDecision` in `lib/cyrus/studios/sound-edit.ts`, re-applied by the preview route).

### What a customer can do (page `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/sound`, `?set=<set>&event=<event>` opens one)
- **Events** (left): every sound set of the mod (from its `CyrusProjectAsset` rows, kind `sound`), mob or item (`setKindOf`: fire/reload roles or a texture of the same name = item), the used events plus the standard unused slots ("Not used · add a sound": mob = ambient/hurt/death/attack/step/spawn, item = fire/reload). Each row: subtitle (or "Subtitle required" in red), variant count, quality dot (browser estimate on the real `sq-1` bar), a sparkle when a Cyrus candidate is open. A save bar: unsaved edit count, undo/redo (Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z), the first save blocker, **Save revision**.
- **Event header**: `set.event` + role, the pack key `<ns>:<set>.<event>`, the **required subtitle** (`aria-required`, inline error; `subtitleProblem` = the validator's rule, 3-60 plain characters) with its lang key, the volume slider (SoundCategory).
- **Variants**: V1..V4 with weights (stepper 1-10), "players hear V1 67% · V2 33%", + Variant (a copy with synth seeds +13), remove.
- **Waveform editor** (`components/cyrus/studios/sound-canvas.tsx`): ruler, the mix players hear (min/max per column), the -1 dBTP ceiling, cyan playhead, zoom 1-8x (buttons, Ctrl+wheel) + scroll, click to play from a point. The SELECTED layer shows its region with **drag handles**: edges = trim (a library layer's left edge moves the in-point `trimStart` and keeps its tail), top corners = fade in/out, the top line = gain (0 to -40 dB), the body = move (offset). Keyboard: arrows move, Alt+arrows trim the end, [ ] fade in, { } fade out, up/down gain. Space plays, L loops. Pure geometry in `dragLayer` / `hitHandle` / `layerSpan` (unit-tested).
- **Layers** (max 4): library sound | synth preset | silence, each with play-solo, a mini waveform, gain / pitch / offset sliders (silence: length / offset), remove. **Variant FX**: low-pass, high-pass, reverb, echo (exactly what `lib/cyrus/sound/dsp` + `render.ts` support). Every edit is clamped to the validator's ranges (`clampLayer`, `setProcessing`), so the studio never produces a spec the server refuses for range reasons.
- **Meters** (right): integrated loudness against the ROLE band (`ROLE_PROFILE`), true peak against -1 dBTP, silence %, length vs the role's max, auto gain, and whether the limiter capped it; the **Checks** tab lists the `sq-1` checks with their real ids (`format`, `true_peak`, `loudness`, `audible`, `silence_ratio`, `dc_offset`, `duration`) + the subtitle row. In the browser these are an ESTIMATE of the same pure chain; **Render and preview** asks the render host for the authoritative file (encoded Ogg on node-2) and its numbers, which then replace the estimate (labelled).
- **Synth** tab: the 8 presets with mini waveforms and play; the real `SYNTH_PARAMS` (range + doc per parameter). With a synth layer selected it edits THAT layer live (preset, params, seed, length); otherwise it builds a new layer ("Add as layer"). Synth audio is rendered in the browser with the pure DSP (original sound, no licence question).
- **Library** tab: the shared `LibraryBrowser kind="sound"` (built-in source only): search with the taxonomy's synonyms, tag chips (mob, weapon, whoosh, hit, gunshot, scream, door, magic, explosion, water, alert, ui), categories, **length and loudness ranges** (manifest seconds / LUFS, server-side `minDur/maxDur/minLufs/maxLufs`), **similar to** (`similarInLibrary`), a detail row with the 64-level loudness outline, tags, descriptors and the licence ledger (`provenance`, `licenceStatus: unverified`), audition, "Add to <event> Vn".
- **History** tab: every saved revision of the set with the current event's waveform re-rendered from that revision's spec and a **waveform diff** (amber marks where a revision differs by > 3 dB per slice, `peakDiff`); Restore = an edit step (saving makes a new revision; nothing is deleted).
- **Prompt dock**: "Edit set.event", the token estimate (Saka, change build; owner default), send. Cyrus answers with a **candidate** (see below).
- **Narrow** (< 760 px container): sets and events with play, subtitle state, quality dot; an open candidate with Play / **Approve** (adds it as a new variant and saves a revision; owner default "review and approve") / Reject. Editing needs a larger screen (said on the page).

### Audition under the licence gate (decision)
- **Synth layers always play** (pure DSP in the browser, `components/cyrus/studios/sound-audio.ts`: WebAudio at 44.1 kHz, `renderInBrowser` = `lib/cyrus/sound/render.ts renderVariant`, memoised).
- **Library audio never comes from a public file.** `POST /api/cyrus/assets/v1/sound/preview { libraryId, trimStart, length, pitch, fadeIn, fadeOut }` -> `audio/wav`, ONLY when `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` AND the plan may use the Sound Library (else 403 `library_not_cleared` / `asset_locked` / `plan_unknown`). The render host makes a SHORT processed preview of ONE layer (`PreviewJob`, `runner.ts runPreview`: sha256 checked, decoded, trimmed, length-capped at 6 s, pitched, faded, mono 44.1 kHz 16-bit WAV; never the raw file), the portal checks it is a RIFF/WAVE of at most 529 KB, and caches it in-process (`lruCache`: 96 entries / 32 MB) under `sha256(PREVIEW_VERSION, RENDER_VERSION, the FILE's sha256, every parameter)`, so a replaced file never serves an old preview. The browser mixes it with `browserVariant`: the layer's own chain already ran on the host, so only gain and offset are applied client-side (proved equal to the host chain in a unit test). The library list's play button auditions the first <= 4 s unpitched.
- **Not cleared** (today's default): library rows show a locked audition button and the banner "Library audition is off until the owner confirms the sound licence. Synth layers play; library layers are drawn from their outline only."; library layers in a mix are silent (the meters say "Browser estimate without N library layers") and drawn from their loudness outline; "Use in project" answers 403 with the licence reason; saving a spec with a library layer is refused (422 `library_not_cleared`, same rule as builds).
- **Dev/test**: `CYRUS_STUDIO_SOUND_RENDER=fake` (non-production only) = `fakeRenderHost()`: the real DSP and measurements in-process, WAV instead of Ogg, and STAND-IN library audio (a synth preset per category at the manifest's length and loudness; it never reads a library file). The UI labels it ("development stand-in host").
- **Waveform peaks (decision)**: `lib/cyrus/sound/library-peaks.json` (46 KB, committed), derived ON node-2 by `scripts/cyrus/sound-peaks.ts` (sha256-checked decode, 64 buckets of max |sample| per file, one base-36 character per bucket on a 48 dB log scale, `lib/cyrus/sound/peaks.ts`). 64 coarse loudness levels carry no phase, pitch or timbre: the sound cannot be rebuilt from them, they are metadata like the manifest's duration and LUFS (already committed), so this is not making the files available. Chosen over fetching peaks through the gated route because outlines are needed exactly when audition is OFF (to place and trim library layers truthfully). NOT legal advice; the owner's licence decision covers the audio, and the outlines can be removed by deleting the file (the UI then draws no outline).

### Save, render, ship
- **Save** (`POST .../projects/:p/sounds/:set/revisions { spec, baseAssetId, expectedHeadId, acceptCandidate?, mode? }`): the server validates exactly like a build (`checkSoundSpec` with the library flag; errors in the studio's words: `humanSpecError`), the per-mod budgets (`withinBudget` over every set as it would be), ownership, optimistic head (409 `stale_head`); then a NEW `CyrusRevision` (kind `asset`, manifest with `assets/sounds/<set>.json` replaced) + a new `CyrusProjectAsset` (kind `sound`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.sound-doc+json`, provenance `{ doc: { v, spec, supersedes, decision }, specSha256, basedOn, ledger (library rows used), render: "next_build" }`). Never an overwrite. `supersedes` is computed on the server.
- **Shipping**: the pack with sounds is rendered by the next build (the render runs there), so the UI says "Servers get it with the next build". **Builds keep studio sound edits** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` optional `studioSoundFor`, wired in `sync-deps.ts`): when a build returns a set spec the studio doc supersedes (the generated spec it was edited from, or a decided candidate), the studio spec is re-checked, rendered and shipped instead, and recorded (origin `edited`, `keptStudioEdit`). Without the dep sync is unchanged (tested).
- **Render and preview** (`POST .../sounds/:set/render { spec, event }`): plan gate, validation, then `renderJobFor` of that one event on the injectable host; returns per variant the audio (base64; Ogg from node-2, WAV from the fake), `measure`, `quality`, render info. Nothing stored. Host off -> 503 `render_off` ("the studio plays its in-browser preview only").

### Candidates (the AI edit interface, same as textures)
`SoundCandidateBackend { request({ set, event, prompt, current }) -> requestId; poll -> pending | ready { spec, specSha256, event, summary } | failed }` (`lib/cyrus/studios/sound-service.ts`). Real: `changeBuildSoundCandidates` (`sound-candidates.ts`) = `createModBuild(user, { baseBuildId: newest NON-candidate build, changeRequest: 'Sound Studio edit of "<set>.<event>": <prompt> ...', assets: ["sound"], model: "saka" })`; its sound row recorded by the normal asset sync is the candidate (`soundCandidateOf` marker; the chain reader lists them as `soundCandidateBuilds`; texture resolution ignores rows written by sound candidates and vice versa). The UI: a dashed "Candidate" variant chip, the candidate bar (A / B with Vn plays yours then Cyrus's; **Replace Vn** and **Add as Vn+1** = partial accept; "Use all" when the candidate has several variants; Reject), its layers shown read only. Accept = an edit step, saved with `acceptCandidate` + `mode` (the server re-reads the candidate, records `decision`, supersedes its spec); Reject (no unsaved edits) = a revision that keeps the set and records the decision. **Fake**: `fakeSoundCandidates` ("sharper and shorter": pitch +2, 15 % shorter, tighter fades, less reverb, brighter low-pass; `CYRUS_STUDIO_CANDIDATES=fake`, non-production). The real backend was NOT run (no paid model). Also fixed for textures: a new texture candidate now builds on the newest non-candidate build (`chain.baseBuildId`), not on an undecided candidate.

### Library "Use in project" for sounds
`POST library/use { projectId, ref: "sound/builtin/<id>", key: <set>, event }`: plan gate (Sound Library), licence gate (fail closed), reserves `<ns>:<set>.<event>` through the engine-core identifier registry, returns the layer (`libraryLayer`: `lib:<id>`, **pitch -1** so a library file never ships unchanged, length <= 1.5 s, 60 ms fade-out) for the open variant. It does NOT save (the editor may hold other edits); the save makes the revision.

### Files
- Pure / client-safe: `lib/cyrus/studios/sound-edit.ts` (model, drags, subtitles, blockers, candidate apply, audition helpers + gate), `lib/cyrus/sound/peaks.ts`. `lib/cyrus/sound/dsp.ts` no longer imports `node:crypto` (`pcmSha256` moved to `pcm-hash.ts`) so the DSP runs in the browser; `runner.bundle.cjs` regenerated (`scripts/cyrus/build-sound-artifacts.ts`).
- Server: `lib/cyrus/studios/sound-model.ts` (sound sets from rows), `sound-service.ts` (save, render, preview + cache, candidates, fakes), `sound-http.ts` (handlers), `sound-candidates.ts` (real backend), `deps.ts` (`studioRenderHost`, `soundCandidateBackend`), `http.ts` (projects view: `soundSets`, `sound` caps, `soundLibrary` metadata; browse sound extras; use branch), `lib/cyrus/sound/{job,host,runner}.ts` (`PreviewJob`, ssh `preview`), `library-peaks.{json,ts}`.
- Routes (all `/api/cyrus/assets/v1`): `GET|POST projects/:p/sounds/:set/revisions`, `POST projects/:p/sounds/:set/render`, `POST projects/:p/sounds/:set/candidates`, `GET .../candidates/:id`, `POST .../candidates/:id/reject`, `POST sound/preview`; `library` and `library/use` extended.
- UI: `components/cyrus/studios/{SoundStudio,sound-canvas,sound-audio}.tsx/ts`, `LibraryBrowser` (sound branch), `StudioLock` (sound rows with play + waveform), `AssetsTab` (sound sets with play + Edit), `studios.css` (`sd-*`), `icons.tsx` (+ pause, loop, synth, silence, volume, scissors, trash, copy from the mockup set).
- No new tables, no migration.

### Tests
- `test/cyrus-sound-studio.test.ts` (39): edit model (clamps, limits, seeds, FX off-thresholds, slots), subtitle rule == validator on samples, blockers, error wording, drags + hit test, candidate apply modes, the browser-mix == host-chain proof, preview request/key, audition gate per plan, peaks round trip + every library id covered, sound-set resolution (candidates, decisions, other-set and texture-candidate rows), service on an in-memory store (new revision, stale head, subtitle 422, library 422 until cleared, plan gate per plan, budgets path), render with the fake host / off / Katara, gated preview (403s, WAV, cache, key binds sha + params, size cap, LRU), candidates over HTTP (request -> poll -> accept with decision; refused for an empty event and for Katara), handlers (404 / 429 / 400 / 503), projects view caps + metadata without file names, library/use (403 until cleared, pitch -1 layer + reserved id, nothing saved), browse (peaks, ranges, similar, Katara denied), sync keeps studio sound edits.
- RAN on node-2 via devhost: `devhost tsc` clean; `devhost test test/cyrus-sound-studio.test.ts` 39/39; all Cyrus suites + `modbuilder-pipeline` 1235/1236 (the one failure, `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts`, passes 31/31 alone and on the base: a batch-timing flake).
- Playwright (`test/e2e/cyrus-sound-studio.e2e.mjs`, how to run: its header): phase A (licence open) 29/29: trim drag shortens the layer, fade-in drag, one step per drag, Silence + Synth add layers, empty subtitle invalid + save blocked with the truthful message, then saved; survives a reload; History lists it; fake candidate -> Replace V1 -> save -> decision in History; narrow approve; licence note + locked audition + preview 403 + "Add" refused; Katara lock + 8 events listed + API 403 (save, candidate); Free narrow lock; unknown plan fails closed; outsider 404 page + API 404. Phase B (cleared, fake host): gated WAV preview 200 `audio/wav` <= 529 KB, "Add" puts a pitch -1 library layer on the variant, Katara 403 even when cleared. The Texture Studio e2e (`cyrus-studios.e2e.mjs`) 24/24 after updating its Saka check (Saka now gets the editor; "included" is on the plans page).
- Screenshots `test/e2e/cyrus-sound-studio.shots.mjs` -> `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/sound-*.png` (two phases; fixtures `scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` + `scripts/cyrus/sound-fixtures.ts`: banshee + glock_9mm SoundSpecs, synth only, `STUDIO_FIXTURE_LIBRARY=1` adds `scream_female_2_648f` to banshee.hurt; a persisted Sound Studio candidate build for banshee.hurt).
- One REAL run on node-2 of the preview job against the library: see "Real runs" below.
- NOT RUN: the real change-build candidate backend (paid model), a real Minecraft client hearing a studio-saved set, the ssh render host from the portal (the preview job ran directly on node-2), Safari (Ogg decoding of real renders: the studio falls back to measurements only if `decodeAudioData` refuses Ogg).

### Remaining gaps vs the mockup (honest)
- The portal frame (248 px sidebar) leaves a 1192 px container at 1440 px, so the columns are 236 / flexible / 320 px (the mockup's 252 / 344 apply from a 1360 px container); the subtitle hint, the layers eyebrow suffix, "players hear" and the FX "Ogg Vorbis on export" note hide below that width.
- The mockup's set header says "mob · zombie (silenced)"; the spec has no base-mob field, so it says "mob".
- The legend sits under the waveform box instead of over it; the library list starts alphabetically (the mockup starts on a chosen group).
- No spectrum view, no pitch-preserving stretch, no per-layer FX (the DSP has none), no new sound SET from scratch in the studio (sets come from builds; empty mods show the library and a "ask Cyrus" hint).
- Keyboard nudges on the waveform are one edit step each (drags are coalesced).

### Owner review
1. The licence decision (unchanged): until `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`, customers hear synth layers only and library layers stay outline-only. 2. The committed library outlines (`library-peaks.json`): OK as metadata, or remove? 3. Sound candidate = change build on Saka (adds a mod version, costs tokens like any change). 4. Studio sound saves reach servers on the next build (no studio-triggered render/publish yet). 5. Where production renders and previews run (`CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` from the portal host to node-2, or a small render service). 6. Review `impl-shots/sound-*.png` before turning on `cyrus_studios_enabled`.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s+'\n')
EOF

Synth audio is rendered in the browser with the pure DSP (original sound, no licence question).

### Audition under the licence gate (decision)
- **Synth layers always play** (pure DSP in the browser, `components/cyrus/studios/sound-audio.ts`: WebAudio at 44.1 kHz, `renderInBrowser` = `lib/cyrus/sound/render.ts renderVariant`, memoised).
- **Library audio never comes from a public file.** `POST /api/cyrus/assets/v1/sound/preview { libraryId, trimStart, length, pitch, fadeIn, fadeOut }` -> `audio/wav`, ONLY when `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` AND the plan may use the Sound Library (else 403 `library_not_cleared` / `asset_locked` / `plan_unknown`). The render host makes a SHORT processed preview of ONE layer (`PreviewJob`, `runner.ts runPreview`: sha256 checked, decoded, trimmed, length-capped at 6 s, pitched, faded, mono 44.1 kHz 16-bit WAV; never the raw file), the portal checks it is a RIFF/WAVE of at most 529 KB, and caches it in-process (`lruCache`: 96 entries / 32 MB) under `sha256(PREVIEW_VERSION, RENDER_VERSION, the FILE's sha256, every parameter)`, so a replaced file never serves an old preview. The browser mixes it with `browserVariant`: the layer's own chain already ran on the host, so only gain and offset are applied client-side (proved equal to the host chain in a unit test). The library list's play button auditions the first <= 4 s unpitched.
- **Not cleared** (today's default): library rows show a locked audition button and the banner "Library audition is off until the owner confirms the sound licence. Synth layers play; library layers are drawn from their outline only."; library layers in a mix are silent (the meters say "Browser estimate without N library layers") and drawn from their loudness outline; "Use in project" answers 403 with the licence reason; saving a spec with a library layer is refused (422 `library_not_cleared`, same rule as builds).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
Sound Studio is built as real React on `feature/cyrus-r9` (worktree /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r9, 10 commits on top of cyrus-r2). Nothing is deployed and nothing is switched on: `cyrus_studios_enabled` is OFF, the library licence flag is unset, sound rendering is off. No dev servers are running.

**What I built**
- **Page** `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/sound` (`?set=&event=`): `components/cyrus/studios/SoundStudio.tsx`, `sound-canvas.tsx`, `sound-audio.ts`.
- **Editor:** event slots, the required subtitle (saving is blocked without it, with the validator's own wording), weighted variants, and a waveform editor with trim, fade, gain and move handles plus playhead, loop and zoom. Also layers (library / synth / silence), variant FX, loudness meters and checks on the real `sq-1` bar and role bands, the synth presets with their real parameters, history with a waveform diff, the A/B candidate bar (replace / add / reject), and the narrow listen-and-approve view.
- **Locked view and Assets tab** now list the sound sets with play and Edit.
- **Server logic:** `lib/cyrus/studios/sound-{edit,model,service,http,candidates}.ts`. A save always adds a new revision; nothing is overwritten.
- **Routes** under `/api/cyrus/assets/v1`: `projects/:p/sounds/:set/{revisions,render,candidates[/:id[/reject]]}` and `sound/preview`. Library browse and `library/use` now handle sounds.
- **Builds keep studio sound edits** (`sync.ts`), the same rule as for textures.

**How audition works under the licence gate**
- Synth layers always play in the browser, using the same sound code as the render host.
- Library audio plays only when `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` and the plan is Saka or the top plan. Each preview is short (at most 6 s), processed on the render host, cached and size-capped — never the raw file.
- While the licence is open (today), library rows are locked with a note saying audition is off until you confirm the licence. Library layers are silent and drawn as an outline. "Use in project" and saving a library layer are both refused.
- The outlines come from `library-peaks.json`: 64 levels per file, made on node-2 and committed. My judgement is that this is metadata, not the audio — that is not legal advice.

**What ran (on node-2)**
- tsc is clean.
- New unit and API tests: 39/39. All Cyrus suites: 1235/1236; the one failure is in `cyrus-admin` and passes 31/31 when run alone.
- Playwright: sound interaction tests 29/29 with the licence off and 6/6 with it on (fake host). The Texture Studio tests pass 24/24 after I updated their Saka check, since Saka now gets the editor.
- A real preview job ran on the actual library on node-2: deterministic output, 63-87 KB, never identical to the source file.

**Not run:** the real Cyrus candidate path (it needs paid model calls; tests used a fake), a real Minecraft client, the portal-to-node-2 render connection, and Safari.

**Comparison with the mockups:** 23 `sound-*` screenshots are in impl-shots. The cleared-library screens match `sound-dark` and `sound-light` closely; the locked, Assets, narrow and candidate screens match too, and they share the Texture Studio's frame. Gaps: at 1440 px the portal sidebar leaves less width, so the columns are narrower (236/320 instead of 252/344) and a few hints hide. The set header says "mob" rather than "zombie (silenced)", the waveform legend sits below the box, and you can't create a new sound set from scratch in the studio.

**For you to review** (details in DOCUMENTATION.md, "Cyrus sound studio UI (R1b)"):
- The library licence decision.
- Whether committing the waveform outlines is acceptable.
- Sound candidates run as change builds on Saka (a new mod version each time).
- Studio saves reach servers only on the next build.
- Where production renders should run.
- The screenshots, before turning on the flag.
